questions.q: A scenario describes a nightly scheduled data load that needs orchestration and retry logic. Which Fabric tool fits best?
options: A Data Factory pipeline
An Eventstream
A KQL database
A Fabric capacity
questions.explain: Pipelines (Fabric Lesson 8) are the orchestrated, typically batch tool for scheduled loads with retry logic.

questions.q: How do pipelines, notebooks, and Dataflows Gen2 typically relate to each other in a Fabric solution?
options: A pipeline can call a notebook or a Dataflow as one of its own activities — they're often steps inside it, not competitors
They are mutually exclusive and can never be used in the same solution
Dataflows always call pipelines, never the reverse
Notebooks replace the need for pipelines entirely
questions.explain: Pipelines are the orchestration layer; notebooks and Dataflows are frequently steps within a pipeline.

questions.q: What happens when a pipeline writes data whose schema doesn't match the target Lakehouse table?
options: Schema enforcement rejects the mismatched write
The table silently accepts and corrupts the data
Fabric automatically deletes the target table
The write always succeeds regardless of schema
questions.explain: Every Lakehouse table is a Delta table under OneLake, so Databricks Lesson 19's schema enforcement applies silently to every Fabric ingestion path.

questions.q: A scenario asks you to aggregate sensor readings into fixed, non-overlapping five-minute buckets. Which windowing concept does this describe?
options: A tumbling window
A sliding window
A session window
A hopping window with overlap
questions.explain: Tumbling windows (Fabric Lesson 30) are fixed-size and non-overlapping — the exact wording in the scenario.

questions.q: Where does an Eventstream typically route its data in a Fabric solution?
options: To an Eventhouse/KQL database, or directly into a Lakehouse
Only to a Power BI report
Only to a Fabric capacity
Only to a Git repository
questions.explain: Eventstreams (Fabric Lesson 19) sit in front of Eventhouse/KQL databases (Fabric Lesson 21) or can route directly into a Lakehouse.
